 CORAM:HONOURABLE MR. JUSTICE CHEEKATI  MANAVENDRANATH ROY  and  HONOURABLE MR.JUSTICE D. M. VYAS  Date : 07/10/2025  ORAL ORDER (PER : HONOURABLE MR. JUSTICE CHEEKATI MANAVENDRANATH ROY)
1.
This application under Section 5 of the Limitation Act is filed seeking condonation of delay of 9 days in preferring the appeal against the judgment of acquittal.

2. Heard Mr.B.K.Raj, learned counsel for the applicant, Ms.Krina Call, learned APP for respondent no.1-State and Mr.Rohit N. Patel, learned counsel for respondent no.2.
3.
The petitioner is the father of the victim girl.

The second respondent was prosecuted for the offence punishable under Sections 376(1), 354(d), 506(1) and 294 (b) of the Indian Penal Code,
1860 and under Sections 6 and 12 of the Protection of Children from Sexual NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/11644/2025 ORDER DATED: 07/10/2025 undefined Offences Act, 2012 for committing Virat Jagannath Shah vs State Of Gujarat on 7 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/57307922/
1 rape on a minor girl, who is the daughter of the petitioner.

sentences.text:
At the conclusion of the trial, eventually,
they were acquitted of the said charges by the impugned judgment of acquittal.

Aggrieved thereby,
the petitioner has preferred an appeal against the said judgment of acquittal.
There is a delay of 9 days in filing the said appeal.

Explaining the said delay, it is stated that the petitioner has initially entrusted the matter to prefer an appeal to one advocate in the trial court and he did not prefer the appeal in time and thereafter, the petitioner lost confidence in him and took back the file and entrusted the matter to the present counsel to prefer an appeal and the said delay of 9 days has taken place due to the said reason and it is not deliberate.
Thus, the applicant has explained the said delay satisfactorily.
The said reason assigned in explaining the delay is not denied and controverted by the second respondent and only formal objection has been taken opposing the application.

4. Therefore, in the said facts and circumstances of the case, we are of the considered view that the petitioner is entitled for condonation of the said delay of 9 days in preferring the appeal to enable him to pursue his appeal.
5. Resultantly, the application is allowed condoning the delay of 9 days in filing the appeal.

Sd/-
(CHEEKATI MANAVENDRANATH ROY, J) Sd/-
(D. M. VYAS, J) ABHISHEK/8 Virat Jagannath Shah vs State Of Gujarat on 7 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/57307922/
